# ADR-0015: The loop pod stops being a container host — OpenShell Kubernetes driver

> **Status:** proposed | **Date:** 2026-07-08

**References:** [ADR-0002](../adr/ADR-0002.md), [ADR-0005](../adr/ADR-0005.md), [ADR-0011](../adr/ADR-0011.md), [ADR-0014](../adr/ADR-0014.md), [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md)

## Context

The openshell backend runs the sandbox as a container nested inside the loop pod via podman. This forces privileged:true on the loop pod, requires podman/buildah/fuse-overlayfs in the loop image, needs KUBERNETES_SERVICE_* env scrubbing, and requires bespoke credential paths. OpenShell ships a Kubernetes driver that runs the sandbox as a sibling pod, already present in the fork commit.

## Decision

Make the compute driver a configuration knob, defaulting in-cluster to the Kubernetes driver. The sandbox becomes a sibling pod instead of a nested container. Five changes: broker reach contract (transport-agnostic hostname resolution), NetworkPolicy update (sandbox reaches broker over real cluster networking), agent-sandbox CRD prerequisite, RBAC updates (ClusterRole for tokenreviews and nodes), and supervisor delivery via init-container. The podman driver stays supported for laptop and EC2 use.

## Consequences

Positive: loop pod stops being a container host. Sandbox gets ordinary Kubernetes scheduling, limits, and GPU admission. The upstream patch retires. Path to privileged:false opens (combined with declarative image builds).

Negative: agent-sandbox CRD serves v1alpha1 (deprecated); driver's README labels its schema "RFC 0005 POC." Sibling pod networking adds real cluster network hops versus localhost. RBAC surface grows (ClusterRole for tokenreviews, nodes).

## Alternatives Considered

### Make compute driver a configuration knob, default in-cluster to Kubernetes; sandbox becomes a sibling pod with broker reach over cluster networking (accepted)


### Keep podman driver as the default, running sandbox as nested container inside the loop pod (rejected)
